title: Binary guard escape
statement: Let $b,j$ be nonnegative integers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word with $j\le |x|$, and let $out$ and $w$ be finite Boolean words. If $|x|<j+(b+1)N$, where $N$ is the natural number whose binary digits are the entries of $w$, then there is a time $T\le (b+5)(|x|+1)+2|w|$ at which the binary guard machine, started on $x$ at input-head position $j$ with output $out$ and counter tape storing $w$, is in the escape state, its output is still $out$, and its input-head position is $|x|+1$. At every earlier time $u<T$, its state is neither the done state nor the escape state.
hypotheses_covered: $|x|<j+(b+1)$ times the natural number represented by the binary digits of $w$
